title: Diet optimization for patients suffering from celiac disease - NutriMATCH-celiac
summary:
Celiac disease is a T-cell-mediated disorder that, according to current understanding, is triggered by prolonged gluten exposure of the small intestinal mucosa. This occurs in the subgroup of patients who are genetically susceptible to celiac disease.
The therapy for celiac disease is a strictly gluten-free diet, which is very challenging for many patients due to the nearly ubiquitous presence of gluten, frequently leading to insufficiently strict adherence to the diet. This, as well as the presence of functional complaints, can lead to residual symptoms despite general attempts to maintain a GFD (gluten-free diet).
Our concept is that these residual symptoms can be treated through specialized nutritional therapy. Two strategies of nutritional education are compared with each other. This should not only establish nutritional education per se in IBD, but also methodically compare two therapeutic options with each other.

interventions.name: Face2face Medical Nutrition Therapy in CeD
30minute PowerPoint-based video on nutritional advice for CeD

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Established diagnosis of CeD
Initial CeD diagnosis >1 year ago
Exclusion criteria:
Change of a celiac disease-relevant therapy within the last 6 weeks
Does not understand informed consent or cannot sign informed consent
Insufficient German language skills
